rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Rāzī gives two readings of the command: sanctify God’s name, or treat “name” as an added expression and sanctify God Himself.
rows.anchor: في قوله : { اسم ربك } قولان

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: On the first reading, the command may forbid applying God’s name to others, as polytheists named an idol al-Lāt and Musaylima called himself the Merciful of Yamāma.
rows.anchor: نزه اسم ربك عن أن تسمي به غيره

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Another reading forbids explaining divine names in ways that imply bodily attributes: “the Most High” is not spatial height, and istiwāʾ is not settling.
rows.anchor: أن لا يفسر أسماءه بما لا يصح ثبوته في حقه سبحانه نحو أن يفسر الأعلى بالعلو في المكان

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The divine name must be protected from casual mention without reverence, humility, or understanding of its meaning.
rows.anchor: أن يصان عن الابتذال والذكر لا على وجه الخشوع والتعظيم

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The command can mean glorify God through the names He revealed and authorized.
rows.anchor: أي مجده بأسمائه التي أنزلتها عليك

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: This reading also means praying by God’s revealed name, unlike the polytheists’ clapping and whistling, and using only names established by revelation.
rows.anchor: لا كما يصلي المشركون بالمكاء والتصدية

rows.speaker: الفراء
rows.claim: Al-Farrāʾ sees no difference in meaning between “sanctify the name of your Lord” and “sanctify by the name of your Lord.”
rows.anchor: قال الفراء : لا فرق بين

rows.speaker: الواحدي
rows.claim: Al-Wāḥidī distinguishes the forms: the one with bi- glorifies God by His name, while the other purifies the name itself from evil.
rows.anchor: قال الواحدي : وبينهما فرق لأن معنى

rows.speaker: أبو مسلم
rows.claim: Abū Muslim takes “name” here to mean attribute, as in the verse about God’s beautiful names.
rows.anchor: قال أبو مسلم : المراد من الاسم ههنا الصفة

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: A second major reading, favored by a group of careful scholars, treats “name” as an added expression: the intended command is to glorify the Lord.
rows.anchor: أما على الوجه الثاني وهو أن يكون الاسم صلة ويكون المعنى سبح ربك وهو اختيار جمع من المحققين

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Arabic convention mentions the name or remembrance of an exalted person instead of naming that person directly.
rows.anchor: ولكن المذكور إذا كان في غاية العظمة لا يذكر هو بل يذكر اسمه

rows.speaker: لبيد
rows.claim: Labīd’s phrase “the name of Peace be upon you” uses “name of Peace” to mean Peace itself.
rows.anchor:
وقال لبيد :
إلى الحول ثم اسم السلام عليكما

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: One meaning of glorifying God is avoiding conduct toward unbelievers that provokes them to insult God.
rows.anchor: ولا تسبوا الذين يدعون من دون الله فيسبوا الله عدوا بغير علم

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Glorifying God in His essence means believing He is neither a substance nor an accident.
rows.anchor: أما في ذاته فأن يعتقد أنها ليست من الجواهر والأعراض

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Glorifying God in His attributes means believing they are neither originated, finite, nor deficient.
rows.anchor: وأما في صفاته ، فأن يعتقد أنها ليست محدثة ولا متناهية ولا ناقصة

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: In His acts, glorification means affirming God’s absolute ownership, which leaves no one entitled to object to His decisions.
rows.anchor: وأما في أفعاله فأن يعتقد أنه مالك مطلق

rows.speaker: المعتزلة
rows.claim: The Muʿtazilites define glorifying God’s acts as affirming that everything He does is good and right, and that He neither does nor approves evil.
rows.anchor: وقالت المعتزلة هو أن يعتقد أن كل ما فعله فهو صواب حسن

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Rāzī’s position is that God should be named only by names established through revelation.
rows.anchor: أما في أسمائه فأن لا يذكر سبحانه إلا بالأسماء التي ورد التوقيف بها

rows.speaker: المعتزلة
rows.claim: The Muʿtazilites permit any name that suggests no deficiency, whether or not revelation authorized it.
rows.anchor: وأما عند المعتزلة فهو أن لا يذكر إلا بالأسماء التي لا توهم نقصا بوجه من الوجوه

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Rāzī says God imposes duties for no benefit to Himself, purely by ownership; the Muʿtazilite view is that duties serve people’s interests.
rows.anchor: بل إما لمحض المالكية على ما هو قولنا ، أو لرعاية مصالح العباد على ما [ هو ] قول المعتزلة

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Some have used this verse to argue that a name is identical with the named entity.
rows.anchor: من الناس من تمسك بهذه الآية في أن الاسم نفس المسمى

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Rāzī says the dispute is poorly framed: if “name” means the word and “named” the entity they differ; if both mean the entity, their identity is tautological.
rows.anchor: فالعاقل لا يمكنه أن يقول : الاسم هو المسمى

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: He suggests the confusion may come from “name” itself being a noun denoting a timeless meaning, leading later scholars to generalize an earlier formulation.
rows.anchor: قولنا : اسم لفظة جعلناها اسما

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: An argument for identity says people do not say “Glory be to the name of God”; therefore this command means glorify the Lord, who is Himself called by a name.
rows.anchor: والرب أيضا اسم فلو كان غير المسمى

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Rāzī rejects that argument as weak because the command can sanctify the name itself, use “name” as an addition, or mean glorify God by His names.
rows.anchor: واعلم أن هذا الاستدلال ضعيف لما بينا في المسألة الأولى

rows.speaker: عقبة بن عامر
rows.claim: A report from ʿUqba ibn ʿĀmir says the Prophet instructed worshippers to use the verse about the Great Lord in bowing and this verse in prostration.
rows.anchor: روى عن عقبة بن عامر أنه لما نزل

rows.speaker: النبي
rows.claim: Reports say the Prophet recited “Glory be to my Lord, the Great” in bowing and “Glory be to my Lord, the Most High” in prostration.
rows.anchor: أنه عليه السلام كان يقول : في ركوعه : «سبحان ربي العظيم

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Some scholars infer from these reports that the command means to pray using the Lord’s name; they also cite the exegetes’ agreement that 30:17 gives prayer times.
rows.anchor: من العلماء من قال : إن هذه الأحاديث تدل

rows.speaker: علي
rows.claim: ʿAlī and Ibn ʿUmar read the command as “Glory be to my Lord, the Most High,” followed by “who created and proportioned”; the wording supplies the commanded glorification.
rows.anchor: قرأ علي عليه السلام وابن عمر : ( سبحان ربي الأعلى

rows.speaker: المجسمة
rows.claim: The anthropomorphists cite “the Most High” to argue that God is elevated in a physical direction.
rows.anchor: تمسكت المجسمة في إثبات العلو بالمكان بقوله :

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Rāzī rejects spatial elevation: a finite God would have a direction above Him, while an infinite body either has impossible infinite dimensions or is composite and contingent.
rows.anchor: والحق أن العلو بالجهة على الله تعالى محال

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The surrounding context concerns praise: remoteness from the world does not merit praise, while supreme power and unique creation do.
rows.anchor: أما قبل الآية فلأن العلو عبارة عن كونه في غاية البعد عن العالم

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The next description, “who created and proportioned,” confirms that “Most High” refers to power rather than physical direction.
rows.anchor: والخالقية تناسب العلو بحسب القدرة لا العلو بحسب الجهة

rows.speaker: الملحدون
rows.claim: Some skeptics claim that “the Great” and “the Most High” imply two lords, one greater than the other.
rows.anchor: من الملحدين من قال : بأن القرآن مشعر

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Rāzī answers that reason establishes one Creator, and this verse never says God is higher than another lord.
rows.anchor: لما دلت الدلائل على أن الصانع تعالى واحد سقط هذا السؤال

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: “The Most High” can mean that God’s majesty, favors, and claims surpass human knowledge, praise, gratitude, and obedience.
rows.anchor: أنه تعالى أعلى وأجل وأعظم من كل ما يصفه به الواصفون

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Alternatively, the title signals God’s freedom from every defect and His superiority over all things in dominion, sovereignty, and power.
rows.anchor: أن قوله { الأعلى } تنبيه على استحقاق الله التنزيه

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: A third option is that al-aʿlā simply means al-ʿālī, just as al-akbar can mean al-kabīr.
rows.anchor: أن يكون المراد بالأعلى العالي كما أن المراد بالأكبر الكبير

rows.speaker: النبي
rows.claim: A report says the Prophet loved this sūra and said that anyone who knew its merit would recite it sixteen times.
rows.anchor: لو علم الناس علم سبح اسم ربك الأعلى

rows.speaker: عائشة
rows.claim: ʿĀʾisha heard a Bedouin leading prayer with a distorted improvised recitation about pregnancy and childbirth, then rebuked him and his companions.
rows.anchor: أن عائشة مرت بأعرابي يصلي بأصحابه فقرأ : ( سبح اسم ربك الأعلى

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: After commanding glorification, God answers the implicit question of how the Lord is known by pointing to His creation and guidance.
rows.anchor: لما أمر بالتسبيح ، فكأن سائلا قال :

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Rāzī calls creation and guidance a major prophetic proof, citing Abraham’s statement that his Creator guides him.
rows.anchor: عن إبراهيم عليه السلام ، أنه قال : { الذي خلقني

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Moses answered Pharaoh’s question about the Lord by describing Him as the giver of each thing’s form and its guide.
rows.anchor: قال موسى عليه السلام : { ربنا الذي أعطى كل شيء خلقه ثم هدى

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The opening revelation first points to creation and then to teaching, showing the same proof through creation and guidance.
rows.anchor: ثم قال : { اقرأ وربك الأكرم الذي علم بالقلم } وهذا إشارة إلى الهداية

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Creation and guidance are especially forceful evidence because their marvels are abundant and humans can observe them closely.
rows.anchor: العجائب والغرائب في هذه الطريقة أكثر

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: If the phrase concerns humans, proportioning may mean giving them an upright, balanced, beautiful form, as in the description of humanity’s best form.
rows.anchor: جعل قامته مستوية معتدلة وخلقته حسنة

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Another human-specific explanation is that people can perform the actions of other animals by means of their varied faculties and tools.
rows.anchor: أما الإنسان فإنه خلق بحيث يمكنه أن يأتي بجميع أفعال الحيوانات بواسطة آلات مختلفة

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: A third human-specific explanation is that God prepared humanity for religious obligations and worship.
rows.anchor: أنه هيأ للتكليف والقيام بأداء العبادات

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: If the phrase concerns all animals, proportioning means giving each the limbs, tools, and senses it needs.
rows.anchor: أعطى كل حيوان ما يحتاج إليه من أعضاء وآلات وحواس

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: If it covers all creation, proportioning means creating each thing as God wills, with perfect order and craftsmanship, since He knows all and can do all possible things.
rows.anchor: خلق ما أراد على وفق ما أراد موصوفا بوصف الأحكام والإتقان

rows.speaker: الجمهور
rows.claim: The majority read qaddara with a doubled dāl: God assigned every thing a known measure.
rows.anchor: قرأ الجمهور : { قدر } مشددة وقرأ الكسائي

rows.speaker: الكسائي
rows.claim: Al-Kisāʾī reads the verb with a light dāl; al-Qaffāl explains it as “owned,” meaning God owns what He created and directs it to its interests.
rows.anchor: وقرأ الكسائي على التخفيف ، أما قراءة

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Some grammarians treat the doubled and undoubled forms as two dialects with the same meaning, citing the variant forms in 77:23.
rows.anchor: ومنهم من قال : هما لغتان بمعنى واحد

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: God apportioned created things in their essences and attributes: their sizes, durations, qualities, positions, beauty, misery, guidance, and misguidance.
rows.anchor: قوله : { قدر } يتناول المخلوقات في ذواتها

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: In the bodily order, proportioning arranges components to receive particular faculties; guidance creates those faculties in organs so their acts produce complete benefit.
rows.anchor: فالتسوية والتقدير عبارة عن التصرف في الأجزاء الجسمانية وتركيبها على وجه خاص

rows.speaker: مقاتل
rows.claim: Mujāhid’s reported explanation from Muqātil is that God guided the male to the female and showed him how to approach her.
rows.anchor: قال مقاتل : هدى الذكر للأنثى كيف يأتيها

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Other commentators understand guidance as showing each creature how to obtain its livelihood and caring for it.
rows.anchor: هداه للمعيشة ورعاه

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Another view is that God guides people to good and evil, happiness and misery, by giving them perception and the ability to pursue benefit and avoid harm.
rows.anchor: هدى الإنسان لسبل الخير والشر والسعادة والشقاوة

rows.speaker: السدي
rows.claim: Al-Suddī says God determined the fetus’s time in the womb and guided it to emerge.
rows.anchor: قال السدي : قدر مدة الجنين في الرحم

rows.speaker: الفراء
rows.claim: Al-Farrāʾ says “guided” implies both guidance and misguidance, with one side omitted, as in the verse mentioning garments that protect from heat.
rows.anchor: قال الفراء : قدر فهدى وأضل

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Some take guidance to mean calling people to faith, as in the statement that the Prophet guides, meaning invites; all people were invited.
rows.anchor: الهداية بمعنى الدعاء إلى الإيمان

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Others understand guidance as God’s acts serving as signs of His oneness, majesty, self-sufficiency, and uniqueness to rational observers.
rows.anchor: وقال آخرون : هدى أي دلهم بأفعاله

rows.speaker: قتادة
rows.claim: Qatāda says God does not compel or command anyone to sin or misguidance, but approves obedience, commands it, and forbids sin.
rows.anchor: وقال قتادة في قوله : { فهدى } إن الله تعالى

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Rāzī groups the explanations into worldly guidance and religious guidance, preferring the latter: after creation, proportioning, and human faculties, “guided” means made responsible and directed to religion.
rows.anchor: والأول أقوى ، لأن قوله : { خلق فسوى والذي قدر }

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: After commanding glorification, God assures the Prophet because complete glorification requires reciting the revealed Qur’an, and he feared forgetting it.
rows.anchor: لما أمر محمدا بالتسبيح فقال : { سبح اسم ربك الأعلى }

rows.speaker: الواحدي
rows.claim: Al-Wāḥidī explains “We shall make you recite” as inspiring the Prophet to read and ensuring he does not forget what he reads.
rows.anchor: قال الواحدي : { سنقرئك } أي سنجعلك قارئا

rows.speaker: مجاهد
rows.claim: Mujāhid, Muqātil, and al-Kalbī report that the Prophet moved his tongue rapidly during revelation from fear of forgetting, before Gabriel had finished reciting.
rows.anchor: قال مجاهد ومقاتل والكلبي : كان عليه السلام إذا نزل عليه القرآن

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: One explanation is that Gabriel will read the Qur’an to the Prophet repeatedly until he memorizes it without forgetting.
rows.anchor: أن جبريل عليه السلام سيقرأ عليك القرآن مرات حتى تحفظه حفظا لا تنساه

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Another explanation is that God will expand the Prophet’s heart and strengthen his resolve so that one reading suffices for lasting memorization.
rows.anchor: أنا نشرح صدرك ونقوي خاطرك حتى تحفظ بالمرة الواحدة حفظا لا تنساه

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: A third explanation links the promise to the opening command: persist in glorification, and God will gather the Qur’an’s knowledge in the Prophet’s heart and ease him to act on it.
rows.anchor: واظب على ذلك ودم عليه فإنا سنقرئك القرآن الجامع لعلوم الأولين والآخرين

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The verse demonstrates prophethood: an unlettered man retained a long scripture without study, repetition, or writing, beyond ordinary capacity.
rows.anchor: كان رجلا أميا فحفظه لهذا الكتاب المطول من غير دراسة ولا تكرار ولا كتبة

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Because this early Meccan sūra predicts an extraordinary future event that occurred, the promise is foreknowledge and a miracle.
rows.anchor: أن هذه السورة من أوائل ما نزل بمكة

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Some read the phrase as a prohibition, treating the final alif as rhyme; the Prophet must not neglect reciting and reviewing, lest he forget except what God wills.
rows.anchor: قال بعضهم : { فلا تنسى } معناه النهي

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The well-known reading is a promise: God will teach the Prophet until he is secure from forgetting, as one might promise clothing so someone will not remain unclothed.
rows.anchor: والقول المشهور أن هذا خبر والمعنى سنقرئك إلى أن تصير بحيث لا تنسى وتأمن النسيان

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Rāzī considers the prohibitive reading weaker: it requires an irregular added alif and makes the verse a command to use study and review rather than a divine promise.
rows.anchor: على خلاف قوله : { لا تحرك به لسانك

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Rāzī adds that forgetfulness is under God’s control, so a prohibition against it must be indirect; the promise gives greater reassurance and honor.
rows.anchor: ذلك القول لا يتم إلا عند التزام مجازات في هذه الآية منها أن النسيان لا يقدر عليه إلا الله تعالى

rows.speaker: الحسن
rows.claim: Al-Ḥasan says the “greatest fire” is Hell, contrasted with the lesser fire of this world.
rows.anchor: قال الحسن : الكبرى نار جهنم

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Another view holds that the afterlife has fires and levels of differing severity, matching the varying gravity of sins; the worst unbelievers enter the greatest fire.
rows.anchor: أن في الآخرة نيرانا ودركات متفاضلة كما أن في الدنيا ذنوبا ومعاصي متفاضلة

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: A third view identifies the greatest fire with the lowest level, where unbelievers suffer, as stated of hypocrites.
rows.anchor: أن النار الكبرى هي النار السفلى

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Some say the verse was revealed about al-Walīd, ʿUtba, and Abī; Rāzī says the wording applies generally, especially since the sequence is rationally established.
rows.anchor: نزلت هذه الآية في الوليد وعتبة وأبي

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Rāzī notes that the mention of the most wretched alongside those who remember and fear raises the question whether a lesser wretched group must exist.
rows.anchor: إن الله تعالى ذكر ههنا قسمين

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: One answer is that a superlative need not imply an actual comparative, as in the verse calling the people of Paradise better settled and rested.
rows.anchor: أن لفظة الأشقى لا تقتضي وجود الشقي إذ قد يجري مثل هذا اللفظ من غير مشاركة

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Another proposed answer takes “the most wretched” simply as “the wretched one who burns,” like “easier” meaning “easy” in another verse.
rows.anchor: المعنى ، ويتجنبها الشقي الذي يصلى

rows.speaker: شاعر غير مسمى
rows.claim: An unnamed poet’s use of “more honored” and “taller” illustrates superlative forms without an implied rival.
rows.anchor:
مثل قول القائل :
إن الذي سمك السماء بنى لنا *** بيتا دعائمه أعز وأطول

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Rāzī’s preferred account distinguishes the knowledgeable, the hesitant, and the obstinate: the knower is happy, the hesitant has some misery, and the obstinate who ignores the call is most wretched.
rows.anchor: الفرق الثلاثة ، العارف والمتوقف والمعاند

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: One reading connects the promise to the preceding warning: success belongs to the person who purifies himself from the stain of unbelief.
rows.anchor: لما ذكر وعيد من أعرض عن النظر والتأمل

rows.speaker: الزجاج
rows.claim: Al-Zajjāj says the phrase means increasing in piety, since the root sense of “pure” includes growing and becoming abundant.
rows.anchor: وهو قول الزجاج : تكثر من التقوى

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The growth-in-piety interpretation is supported by the declaration of success for believers characterized by humility in prayer.
rows.anchor: قد أفلح المؤمنون الذين هم في صلاتهم خاشعون

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: It is also supported by the opening description of the God-conscious as successful.
rows.anchor: وأولئك هم المفلحون

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Rāzī favors purification from unbelief because the verse does not name what to purify from, so the earlier context supplies it.
rows.anchor: لما لم يذكر في الآية ما يجب التزكي عنه علمنا أن المراد هو التزكي عما مر ذكره قبل الآية

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: He adds that an unrestricted term denotes its fullest instance, and the fullest purification is removing unbelief’s darkness from the heart.
rows.anchor: وأكمل أنواع التزكية هو تزكية القلب عن ظلمة الكفر فوجب صرف هذا المطلق إليه

rows.speaker: ابن عباس
rows.claim: Ibn ʿAbbās explains “purifies himself” as saying, “There is no god but God.”
rows.anchor: روي عن ابن عباس أنه قال معنى : { تزكى } قول :
